Short note — we've seen this crop up when Calendly's timezone autodetect falls back to the scheduling page owner's browser timezone if the invitee's browser blocks geolocation. Two workarounds that have worked:

1) Send a manual .ics generated in the target timezone; recipients' calendars usually honor the DTSTART TZID when importing.
2) Send a link to a hosted ICS (or attach) + explicit timezone text, and optionally a Chili Piper fallback that forces TZ.

I'll prepare an .ics for Mon Oct 19 20:00 CET and Jasmine can send it as the canonical invite. Also attaching a tiny diagnostic .ics I use for testing.

Attachment: debug-timezone.ics (text/calendar)

— Ben
